$SPY $BA $LMT  Saab Drops A Bombshell Offer To Canada, Gripen Factory If Ottawa Rejects F-35 
 
Sweden’s Saab has offered Canada a major incentive, select the Gripen and Saab would establish a fighter production centre in Canada. 
 
That could put Canadian workers and aerospace companies directly into the Gripen production chain while giving Ottawa a larger industrial stake in its future fighter fleet.  
 
The offer comes as Canada weighs its future combat aircraft and the strategic implications of choosing Sweden’s Gripen over the U.S. made F-35. 
 
This is no longer just a fighter competition, it could become a battle over Canada’s next generation of aerospace jobs and industry.

LightPath Technologies slips as Army widens search for NGSRI suppliers 
 
LightPath Technologies (LPTH) is under pressure on Friday after the U.S. Army signaled it is casting a wider net for companies that could support its effort to replace the Stinger missile. Lockheed Martin (LMT) and RTX's (RTX) Raytheon remain the lead contractors developing prototypes for the Next Generation Short Range Interceptor program, and LightPath currently provides the infrared imaging tech used in Lockheed's design. But in an August 26 notice, the Army said it plans to evaluate additional potential sources ahead of a planned spring 2027 demonstration, a milestone that could ultimately determine who wins the procurement award.

messages.body: $SOXX $SPY $QQQ What would happen to $LMT if they raise interest rate..!!👀

$LPTH Crazy reaction here.  The Army could still proceed with Lockheed and/or RTX separately. But the AID notice creates the possibility that: 
 
- One of Lockheed or RTX is selected for the primary path, while the Army develops another source.  Anduril, likely candidate, who is a major customer of $LPTH  
 
- Both Lockheed and RTX continue, with additional competitors introduced. 
 
- The Army delays a major production commitment until it sees the Spring 2027 demonstration. 
 
The program evolves into a multi-vendor procurement, rather than winner-take-all.  Seems like a way for army to negotiate lower price with LMT & RTX.  Not sure how realistic it is to give a new entrant 6 months to develop a solution when it has taken $RTX and $LMT years to get to this point and expect to make a decision right after the spring demos.  
 
- OR, Anduril? replied to that RFP from July and offered something worth considering and opened this back up for competition??

data.description: Poland has signed the largest arms loan in European Union history, drawing 43.7 billion euros in credit from the bloc's new 150-billion-euro rearmament instrument known as SAFE. Warsaw moved ahead of eighteen other applicants to secure the single largest allocation, with the first 6.6 billion euros disbursed on May 29 - the first SAFE money paid to any member state.
